articles.summary: Second annual report highlights national accreditation, child development findings and partnerships that help families access care Key takeaways: External standards support quality accountability: 86% of KinderCare centers and programs were nationally accredited in 2025. KinderCare is examining employee and family engagement to identify practices associated with stronger center performance. articles.summary: Champions joins Lights On Afterschool to advocate for sustainable child care funding and expand access to quality before- and after-school programs for working families Key takeaways Families need greater access to affordable before- and after-school care. Demand continues to exceed available space in programs, leaving families navigating gaps between the school day and workday. Federal child care funding plays a critical role in supporting school-age families. About 44% of children served through the Child Care and Development Fund are school-age, demonstrating the importance of child care funding beyond early childhood. Champions helps bridge the gap for families. Champions works with school districts, communities and policymakers to expand families' access to high quality before- and after-school programs. articles.summary: New findings highlight disconnect between working parents’ child care needs and employer benefits as families prepare for the holidays Key takeaways Study core finding: According to the 2026 KinderCare Confidence Index, conducted with The Harris Poll, 68% of parents want on-demand or emergency child care, but only 38% report that their employers offer it, a 30-percentage-point gap. Why it matters: 81% of parents are constantly thinking about potential child care disruptions, and unreliable care affects employment: 50% have missed work, 35% have reduced their hours, and two-thirds say it has negatively affected their work performance. Employer opportunity: Parents also want broader child care options and subsidies than employers currently provide. KinderCare helps more than 700 organizations address these needs through backup care, tuition benefits, on-site and near-site care, and before- and after-school programs. articles.summary: Mike Nuzzo steps down; David Barse to head Audit Committee; Preston Grasty rejoins Board KinderCare Learning Companies, Inc. (“KinderCare”) (NYSE: KLC), a leading provider of high-quality early childhood education and care, today announced that Mike Nuzzo has resigned from the company’s Board of Directors, effective Sept. 28, due to other personal and professional time commitments. David Barse, who joined KinderCare’s Board on Aug. 3, replaces Nuzzo as the Head of the Audit Committee. Preston Grasty, Senior Investment Leader at Partners Group, has rejoined the Board, effective Sept. 29. “On behalf of the entire Board and KinderCare, I want to thank Mike for his years of dedicated service to our company,” said Tom Wyatt, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of KinderCare. “We are deeply grateful for his commitment to KinderCare and our mission to give children the very best start in life, and we wish him all the best. I’m excited to welcome Preston back to our board.” About KinderCare
